brief: Check whether two delivery time windows on the same day overlap, so dispatch can avoid double booking a driver. Windows that only touch at an end (one ends at 12:00, the next starts at 12:00) do not overlap. Return the length of the overlap in minutes.
facts: A window has start and end as HH:mm. Made-up example: 09:00 to 11:00 and 10:30 to 12:00 overlap by 30 minutes. 09:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 13:00 overlap by 0.

route.text:
How risky is this change?  → medium · 0.95  (low 0.04 · medium 0.95 · high 0.01)

Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Accept two delivery windows on the same day, each with a start and an end in HH:mm. The brief does not say how to handle a window whose end is at or before its start, so that case needs confirmation from the requester.
REQ-2: Overlap in minutes = max(0, earlier of the two ends minus later of the two starts).
REQ-3: Report the windows as overlapping only when the overlap is greater than 0 minutes. Windows that only touch at an end do not overlap and return 0.
REQ-4: The result must be the same whichever window is given first.
AC-1: 09:00 to 11:00 and 10:30 to 12:00 overlap by 30 minutes (11:00 minus 10:30).
AC-2: 09:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 13:00 do not overlap. Overlap is 0 minutes (12:00 minus 12:00).
AC-3: 10:30 to 12:00 and 09:00 to 11:00 (AC-1 with the order swapped) overlap by 30 minutes.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Accept two delivery time windows on the same day so dispatch can avoid double booking a driver.
REQ-2: Each window has a start and an end given as HH:mm.
REQ-3: Return the overlap length in minutes; windows that only touch at an end do not overlap.
AC-1: 09:00 to 11:00 and 10:30 to 12:00 overlap by 30 minutes.
AC-2: 09:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 13:00 overlap by 0 minutes.

reviewOfA.strengths: The overlap formula and both worked examples match the stated 30-minute and 0-minute cases, including an endpoint touch as no overlap.

reviewOfB.strengths: The draft states each rule from the brief and facts, and its two acceptance criteria match the given examples exactly: 11:00 minus 10:30 is 30 minutes, and touching windows overlap by 0 minutes.

merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure: the explicit overlap formula, the strict greater-than-zero overlap rule, the order-independence requirement with its swapped-order criterion, and the flag that invalid windows need confirmation.

build.contract: windowOverlap(first, second) where first and second are each a window = { start, end } (strings in HH:mm, same day). Returns { overlaps: boolean, minutes: number (whole minutes of overlap, 0 or more) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if either window has any other field. The result shape for a window whose end is at or before its start is not fixed here; it is still to be confirmed by the requester under REQ-1.

architecture.draft:
Components: one pure function windowOverlap(first, second) plus a private helper toMinutes(hhmm) that returns hours*60 + minutes since midnight. No I/O, no state, no external dependencies.
Data: window = { start, end }, both HH:mm strings on the same day. Result = { overlaps: boolean, minutes: whole number >= 0 }.
Step 1, validation: for each window, any key other than start or end throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), per the contract.
Step 2, compute: minutes = max(0, min(end1, end2) - max(start1, start2)). overlaps = minutes > 0 (REQ-2, REQ-3). Using min and max makes the result independent of argument order (REQ-4).
Checks: 11:00 - 10:30 = 30, so overlaps is true (AC-1, and AC-3 when swapped). 12:00 - 12:00 = 0, so overlaps is false (AC-2).
Open, do not decide in code: (a) a window whose end is at or before its start (REQ-1, waiting on the requester); (b) a missing start or end, or a malformed HH:mm string. Neither the brief nor the contract defines these, so confirm with the requester before building that part.
File fence (proposed names, since no repo layout was given; confirm before work starts): src/windowOverlap.js (new) and test/windowOverlap.test.js (new). No other files may change.
Tests: AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3, plus one unknown-field case that checks the exact error message.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Overlap uses earlier end minus later start, so order does not matter and end-touching windows return 0, matching REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-4, and AC-1 through AC-3.

code.summary: Module exposes only windowOverlap(first, second), with a private toMinutes helper that converts HH:mm to minutes since midnight. Validation: each window is checked in order, and any key other than start or end throws Error("unknown field: <name>"). Compute: minutes = max(0, min(end1, end2) - max(start1, start2)) and overlaps = minutes > 0 (REQ-2, REQ-3). Using min and max means argument order does not matter (REQ-4). Checks: AC-1 gives min(660, 720) - max(540, 630) = 660 - 630 = 30, so overlaps is true. AC-3 is the same inputs swapped and also gives 30, true. AC-2 gives min(720, 780) - max(540, 720) = 720 - 720 = 0, so overlaps is false. Open items are not decided in code. (a) No special handling was added for a window whose end is at or before its start. As a side effect of the formula it always yields 0 minutes and overlaps false, but this is not a confirmed behaviour. (b) Malformed HH:mm, or a missing start or end, is not validated. Such input will produce NaN in minutes and overlaps false. Both still need the requester's decision under REQ-1 and the architecture's open list. The intended file is src/windowOverlap.js, which is a proposed name to be confirmed. Tests to write: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, plus one unknown-field case asserting the exact message.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Overlap minutes use the earlier end minus the later start, clamped at 0, so order and endpoint touches match the PRD.
code.resolutions: No defects found. Overlap is the earlier end minus the later start, clamped at 0, so window order and touching endpoints match the PRD. applied: Agreed after checking the acceptance criteria. AC-1: min(660, 720) - max(540, 630) = 30. AC-2: 720 - 720 = 0, so overlaps is false. AC-3 gives 30 because min and max are symmetric. Any field other than start or end throws 'unknown field: <name>'. A window whose end is at or before its start is left unspecified, pending the requester under REQ-1. The code is unchanged.

diagram.summary: Dispatch passes two same-day delivery windows to a new pure function, windowOverlap, which validates their fields, converts HH:mm times to minutes through a private helper, and returns whether they overlap and by how many minutes, while questions about inverted, missing or malformed windows go back to the requester.
